minimalCompletenessFindings: Ten of the 18 submissions pass by the published sum. A fully numerical quotient in N with a physical direction is sufficient in one line. Formula-only and qualitative-only responses each earn 3/10. A correct signed calculation in N without direction earns exactly 8, while the same work without the force unit earns 7.5. Thus the unit decides that boundary even though both omit interpretation. A maintained claim that negative means right would also leave 8 with otherwise correct work, because it loses only the 2 interpretation points. The general subtraction order plus an otherwise correct result reaches 8.5 without numerical change evidence. Both unsupported inferences from average to instantaneous behavior reach 8.5. In contrast, the explicit multiplication error earns 7.5, the maintained endpoint-addition error earns 7, and the isolated subtraction slip earns 9.5 with full follow-through.
